{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement — verified findings 
**Privileged & confidential — attorney work product**

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified nineteen findings: two critical, seven high, seven medium and two low. Six positions are already compliant and need no edit (exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitments and, on the facts, vendor audit rights).

The two critical items are: (i) **Section 13 vests all IP in Garman, including the bespoke Modifications we commission and pay for under Schedule "D"**, and the Agreement is silent on ownership of our data even though Section 4(b) has Garman converting it; and (ii) **Section 15 contains no monetary aggregate cap at all**, leaving direct-damages exposure unlimited on both sides. Section 15 does already carry a mutual consequential-damages exclusion and carve-outs for Sections 13 and 14, so the fix is additive rather than a rewrite.

The high-severity cluster concerns exit and portability: a blanket mutual assignment bar (Section 20(d), reinforced by Sections 2 and 3(c)) with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard; a licence grant limited to affiliates at Authorized Locations with no contractor or successor-transfer rights; a mutual one-year **no-hire** in Section 19 covering all personnel; and an IP indemnity in Section 13 that indemnifies but does not defend, omits our affiliates, has no claim-handling procedure and imposes a hard ten-day notice condition. Medium items are gap-fillers and forum: no maintenance renewal mechanics or fee-uplift cap, no transition assistance or data return on termination, a ninety-day convenience notice with no prepaid-fee refund, no remedy attached to the Section 12 warranty, and Nova Scotia governing law with non-exclusive venue. Vendor insurance is absent entirely despite on-premises installation and data conversion.

One finding — the AUDIT analysis — failed automated verification and is carried as **needs_review** pending human sign-off; substantively the Agreement grants Garman no audit right against us, which is better than our preferred position, so we propose no edit.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman owns all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto", i.e. the paid-for Modifications; no data-ownership provision at all. Limit Garman's ownership to its pre-existing Work, vest paid-for Modifications in us with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back to embedded Garman IP, confirm we own our data (including converted data), exclude joint ownership. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary aggregate cap; direct-damages exposure unlimited for both parties. Insert a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims (retaining §§ 13 and 14; adding data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and fee obligations excluded from the cap. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(d); see also §§ 2, 3(c), 17) | Blanket mutual assignment bar, no affiliate/M&A carve-out for us, no reasonableness standard, no change-of-control right. Add affiliate/successor carve-out, reasonableness on consent, bar on assignment to our competitors, and confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination, suspension or re-pricing right; conform § 3(c). |
| 4 | High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Indemnity exists and is carved out of the § 15 cap, but is hold-harmless only (no defence duty), omits our affiliated companies, has no claim-handling procedure, imposes a hard 10-day notice with no prejudice qualifier, and covers only IP warranty breach. Add one paragraph supplying defence, affiliate coverage, notice/control/cooperation mechanics and triggers for breach of law, unauthorized access/disclosure of our data or Confidential Information, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Perpetual term is compliant, but the grant reaches only affiliates "operating at Authorized Locations", omits contractors acting on our behalf, and is expressly non-transferable with no successor path. Extend to affiliates and contractors, add successor-transfer right, conform §§ 3(c) and 20(d). |
| 6 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Mutual, but drafted as a **no-hire** covering any employee of the other party with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Narrow to a 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services (running from end of involvement) with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | Only non-exclusive licence/escrow grants, exclusive-remedy and non-exclusive jurisdiction references; no exclusive-dealing or sole-supplier commitment. No edit. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment or early-termination charge; §§ 8, 17(b) and 17(c) run refunds and exit rights in our favour. No edit. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | § 3 is limited to conventional licence-scope restrictions; § 19 is a non-solicitation, and § 14 carves out independently developed information. No edit. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 | Nova Scotia/Canadian law with non-exclusive Nova Scotia jurisdiction; no arbitration required. Move to New York law and exclusive state and federal courts in New York County; Delaware/California or England and Wales (London) as fallbacks. |
| 11 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Missing | § 10 Maintenance and Support | Only a "renewable one-year term"; no renewal length, opt-out window, reminder or uplift cap. Add successive 12-month renewals, 30-day customer opt-out, 60-day Garman reminder, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% (fallback 5%/60 days). |
| 12 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 17 Term and Termination | Our convenience right sits at fallback only: 90 days' notice and no refund of prepaid fees (the 17(c) refund applies only on Garman default; § 8 only on rejection). Shorten to 30 days and add pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. |
| 13 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17 covers only our return/destruction obligations; no transition assistance, no return of our data, no deletion or certification. Insert new § 17(d) (six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification) and add to the § 18 survival list. |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Duration is compliant and there is no "AS IS" disclaimer, but no remedy is stated (only "best efforts" fee-bearing repair under maintenance), and services, no-malicious-code and compliance-with-laws warranties are absent. Add those warranties plus repair/replace/re-perform with refund if Garman fails to cure within 30 days. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN or pricing-parity provision in either direction. No edit. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 Fees | Fees payable only for licence and services taken; additional-location fees are elective; maintenance is a renewable one-year term; § 17(b) exit available. No edit. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Page 11 (§ 20 General Matters) | No insurance covenant anywhere, despite on-premises installation under § 4(a) and conversion of our data under § 4(b), and with Garman's liability limited by § 15. Insert new § 20(k): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request, surviving one year post-term (fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). |
| 18 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 3 Restrictions on Use | Garman holds no audit, inspection, records or system-access right against us — better than our preferred position — so the minimal edit is no edit. The automated "audit frequency limited" check cannot pass without manufacturing an audit right; flagged for human override. If Garman later proposes any verification or usage-reporting clause, insert the preferred parameters into § 3 then. |

## Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as playbook walk-away positions and should be resolved before signature:

1. **Assignment (Page 10, § 20(d)).** A blanket assignment prohibition with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us and no reasonableness standard on consent is the playbook walk-away position, compounded by § 3(c) and the "non-transferable" grant in § 2.
2. **Non-solicitation (§ 19).** No-hire provisions, and restrictions extending to all Vendor personnel regardless of involvement, are walk-away items. We have proposed narrowing rather than deletion.
3. **Vendor insurance (Page 11).** No insurance for a vendor that processes our data and works on our premises is the walk-away position; the gap is aggravated by the § 15 limitation of Garman's liability.

For completeness, the findings confirm the **indemnity** walk-away triggers (indemnity absent / IP excluded) are **not** met, because § 13 contains a Garman-side IP indemnity with procure/modify/replace remedies, no fee-only refund escape, a § 15 carve-out and § 18 survival.

## Next steps

1. **Priority redlines to Garman:** IP ownership of paid-for Modifications and our data (§ 13) and the mutual liability cap with Excluded Claims (§ 15). These two drive the commercial risk profile and should lead the markup.
2. **Second tier:** assignment/change of control (§ 20(d), conforming § 3(c)), licence scope for affiliates, contractors and successors (§ 2), the § 13 indemnity paragraph (defence, affiliates, procedure, misconduct triggers), and the § 19 non-solicit narrowing.
3. **Gap-fillers to table together:** maintenance renewal mechanics and uplift cap (§ 10), transition assistance, data return and certified deletion as new § 17(d) with § 18 survival, 30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund (§ 17(b)), warranty remedies and additional warranties (§ 12), and the insurance covenant as new § 20(k).
4. **Forum:** propose New York law and exclusive New York County courts; hold Delaware/California or England and Wales (London) in reserve as fallbacks.
5. **Internal confirmations needed:** (a) business sign-off on the fallback insurance limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) if Garman cannot meet the preferred limits; (b) sign-off on the renewal uplift fallback (5% / 60 days); and (c) reviewer override on the AUDIT finding, which failed automated verification — we recommend confirming "no edit" so we do not manufacture an audit right against us.
6. **No action** on exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, MFN and minimum commitments; these are compliant and we will not open them.
"}
